location: pp. 1145-1146 (Results; Figs. 2c, 3a); Supplementary Fig. 5; Supplementary Table 1
quote_or_reading: "Across the full population, 22% of RSC cells had turn-bias ratios greater than 2, and 45.6% of RSC neurons exhibited significant differences in overall left-turn versus right-turn firing rates (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, n = 104 of 228 neurons at P < 0.05" (p. 1145); "54.3% of RSC neurons (n = 124 of 228, Wilcoxon rank-sum test, P ≥ 0.05) did not have significant left-turn versus right-turn firing rate differences (Fig. 3a,b). notes: No RSC field widths or field counts: "there was little evidence for single, isolated firing fields of the type typically observed for HPC neurons" (p. 1147). Subregion counts are in Supplementary Table 1, an image not read. Same W track and rats as alexander2015_2 and _3 and the kernel rows alexander2015_k1 to _k4.

citation: Alexander AS, Nitz DA (2015). Retrosplenial cortex maps the conjunction of internal and external spaces. Nat Neurosci 18:1143-1151
strain: Male Long-Evans rats, 4 of the 6 with a CA1 drive
level_definition: CA1 microdrive at A/P -3.8 mm, M/L ±2.3 mm, D/V -0.5 mm (Online Methods, PDF p. 10); dorsal CA1 by coordinates
environment_size: W-shaped track with 2 cm edges; each route 215 cm with turns at 60, 110 and 170 cm (LRL outbound, RLR inbound); run at two room locations (alpha, beta) and then again at alpha (alpha-prime); room 13.5 ft x 13.5 ft, about 4.1 m (Supplementary Fig. 1)
familiarity: Habituated to the track for 2 weeks, then ran both routes rapidly before recording; sessions about 45 min; at least 5 and on average 16 uninterrupted runs per route and track location
field_rule: Same template as the RSC rows. CA1 cells kept if mean rate <= 8 Hz across track sessions, a bin above 3 Hz and >= 150 spikes, and only cells with a place field: peak >= 5 Hz over >= 20 adjacent template bins (about 24 cm)
measure: CA1 comparison population: inclusion rule and turn-bias reliability
value_reported: 109 CA1 neurons with place fields; 39 had significant left vs right turn rate differences, with a preferred-turn CV of 1.50 ± 0.53 (randomized 1.57 ± 0.42, p = 0.24) against 0.52 ± 0.33 for the 104 RSC turn cells

notes: No CA1 field widths are reported; the minimum field length is about 24 cm by rule. The authors read the 39 turn-biased CA1 cells as "unidirectional place fields that happened to overlap with a turn site". Kernel of these cells: alexander2015_k3.

strain: Male Long-Evans rats, 3 of the 5 with a CA1 drive
level_definition: CA1 microdrive at A/P -3.8 mm, M/L ±2.3 mm, D/V -0.5 mm (STAR Methods p. e2); dorsal CA1 by coordinates
environment_size: Closed plus-shaped track run clockwise, 12 equal segments; Fig. 1B labels one segment 55 cm, so a lap is about 660 cm (derived, nominal; rats cut the corners, Fig. 1B right); 1 cm edges, open view of the room; reward at the arrow point. field_rule: Same template as the RSC rows. CA1 cells excluded if mean rate > 8 Hz, no bin falling to 0 Hz, or no bin above 3 Hz (STAR Methods p. e2); no place-field rule or width
measure: CA1 comparison population and its reconstruction errors
value_reported: 141 CA1 "place cells" in 3 rats; odd vs even position reconstruction error 5.2 ± 6.7 cm against 1.9 ± 2.7 cm for 229 RSC cells; distance-from-symmetry-point reconstruction error 12.61 cm against 2.93 cm for RSC
location: p. 1552 (Results; Fig. 1D); p. 1556 (Fig. 4E); STAR Methods p. e2
quote_or_reading: "Such ''reconstruction'' of the animal's progression along the route was accurate to 1.9 ± 2.7 cm based on RSC populations, a value comparing favorably to the accuracy seen for 141 hippocampal CA1 ''place cells'' recorded in three animals (Figures 1C and 1D; CA1 accuracy = 5.2 ± 6.7 cm mean ± SEM)" (p. 1552); "Mean distance reconstruction error for RSC was 2.93 cm, significantly lower than that observed for HPC (µHPC = 12.61 cm; Wilcoxon rank-sum test; n = 72" (p. 1556)
notes: No CA1 or RSC field widths are reported. The ± after 5.2 is labelled SEM; with a mean of 5.2 it is more likely an SD (inference). Kernel of these cells: alexander2017_k2. Symmetry points were uniform in RSC but biased in CA1 (Rayleigh p = 0.03).

strain: Male Long-Evans rats, 2 of the 5 (the same 2 also ran the W track of Alexander & Nitz 2015)
level_definition: Microdrives at A/P -5.8 mm, M/L ±0.7-1.2 mm, D/V -0.5 mm, 10-12° angle (STAR Methods p. e2); Fig. 1A sections at -5.52, -5.76 and -6.36 mm, "caudal RSC"; cells in Rd and Rg (Fig. S1B). Rule: posterior half of rat RSC (about AP -1 to -8)
